top_choice_rationale: P005 (Cullis, Hope, Madden) credits a coherent set of physical-chemical design rules for a self-assembled system: pH-dependent ionizable lipids that entrap nucleic acid and are near-neutral in circulation, then re-charge in the endosome and drive non-bilayer phase behaviour and release. The principle has been reproduced independently and underlies approved siRNA and mRNA medicines at very large scale, so maturity is strongest on the slate. The credit cap leaves out Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan, which I accept as the main weakness. I rank the degrader proposals next because they carry the stronger novelty claim, with the Handa variant (P002) above the Ciulli variant (P003) since cereblon supplies clinical proof, and C-N coupling (P001) below them because it is a mature but less conceptually new extension of a known catalytic cycle.
recusal_note: Possible conflict: my research on lipid self-assembly, phase behaviour and membranes is close to the field of the P005 proposal, and I am a Lund colleague of Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai; no direct collaboration with any proposed laureate is apparent from the profile.
